title: A thrift stop for the cats.
summary: A family thrift stop at Safe Haven in Wells, with a $1 L.L.Bean find, a vintage school-dance shirt recommendation and a free board for future browsing.
search: The journal / Out & about / Wells, Maine Safe Haven · Wells, Maine A thrift stop for the cats. Our favorite $1 L.L.Bean find, a vintage Tommy Jeans velour shirt for James’s upcoming school dance, and a fellow thrifter’s directions to the clearance walls. A family stop at Safe Haven in Wells, with practical notes and a free board for a future browse. October 18, 2026 · From the family camera roll A Sunday stop at Safe Haven, with autumn flowers by the door. The little storyThe $1 tipAccess & the upstairs routeFree choice boardPlan a visit Our favorite find at Safe Haven in Wells was L.L.Bean for $1. We also met a lovely, inveterate thrifter who recommended a vintage Tommy Jeans velour shirt for James, with his upcoming school dance in mind. Retro cool was the idea. He told us Safe Haven was the absolute best store he goes to, then pointed out the $1 clearance walls along the side and back of the store. That is the sort of recommendation I like: directions to the dollar section and an eye for a school-dance shirt. Our October camera roll has plenty else to look at. Floral lamps in a sunny window. Wicker chairs. A patchwork quilt draped over a wooden stand. Baskets, cushions, old records and shelves that reward a second look. This is a shop with quite a lot going on. The lamps and wicker department, making a case for looking closely.Quilts, cushions, baskets—and quite a few possible distractions. The antiques continue upstairs. In our photographs, a large lighted Christmas tree stands beside the wooden staircase. The flowers outside are still firmly in October; the tree has started work early. And then there is the sign on the door: Don’t let the cats out, no matter what they tell you! A very clear instruction, with room for the possibility that the cats have prepared an argument. The cats are the reason behind the shopping. Safe Haven says proceeds from its Vintage/Thrift/Antique Shop at Cattail Farm help fund its all-volunteer cat rescue, rehabilitation, adoption and care work in York County. A useful place to browse, with a purpose beyond the next set of shelves. A tip passed along in the shopAsk about the $1 clearance walls.A fellow shopper pointed us to the clearance walls along the side and back of the store. Ask which areas are marked $1, then check each item’s label.For a clothing browse, check size, care instructions, seams and fastenings before deciding. Ask what can be browsed on the entrance level if stairs do not work for your visit. Closely arranged displaysFurniture, baskets and breakable items sit close together in some photographed areas. We have not measured aisle widths or turning space. Ask about the route for a wheelchair, walker or stroller before relying on it. Arrival and a place to pauseThe exterior photographs show asphalt in front of the shop, with merchandise near the entrance. They do not establish a complete step-free route, accessible parking or a usable restroom. Confirm the details you need and choose a place to pause with your group. title: The support-professional field notes
summary: Practical field notes for direct support professionals, personal assistants and paid caregivers: a clear start, everyday choices, professional boundaries and useful handovers.

An activity idea here does not authorise a care procedure.Begin with the person, then the plan.A useful starting point +Duties, training and employer requirements vary; use current arrangements.Read the full details Build around a chosen piece of ordinary life.Room for the personBuild around a chosen piece of ordinary life.The useful errand Agree one destination and what the person wants to do there. Check the transport, access, spending arrangements and return plan. Support the person’s part of the errand without taking over every decision.
